entries.qualification: Initial planning handoff. It used one READY name and did not distinguish cap-free code preflight from post-registration authoritative-bootstrap readiness. Never implemented or accepted.

Second planning handoff. It introduced CODE_READY/BOOTSTRAP_READY but had not yet bound DAG context/result to the stable subscriber or registered sealed/start phases for Flow-scope cleanup. Never implemented or accepted.

Third planning handoff. It fixed readiness, stable subscriber identity and Flow-scope cleanup, but did not yet name the success-only DAG EOF routes or bind failed producer closure to the signed terminal event. Never implemented or accepted.

Fourth planning handoff. It added dedicated success-only DAG EOF routes and signed-event failure authority, but did not explicitly require the routed adapter to override the inherited legacy reject_output/fail_task_output hooks. Never implemented or accepted.
Fifth planning handoff. It named DAG finish and failure-hook overrides but had not yet classified every inherited PrefectStreamStorage business method. Never implemented or accepted.

Sixth planning handoff. It completed the inherited storage-method matrix but did not yet name the existing entrypoint child lease calls that conflict with worker/graph-owned DAG lease authority. Never implemented or accepted.
Current planning handoff. It completes the storage matrix and requires DAG-specific entrypoint wiring to skip/replace legacy child lease renew/release calls while preserving fixed-P2 behavior.

reason: The existing entrypoint reports cap-free preflight readiness before receiving and validating the private/authoritative bootstrap. Reusing that witness for activation would permit an incompletely bound child to cross the graph barrier. A second runtime review found that legacy operator loops expose TaskRun.id as consumer identity and that no Flow-scope registry owned a sealed preview or partially started graph. A further integration review found that the routed adapter inherited legacy source/consumer finish methods; the current handoff now requires dedicated success-only DAG EOF routes and signed-event failure closure. The routed adapter also inherits legacy rejection hooks, so the current handoff explicitly requires overriding and denying them for DAG execution. A complete inherited-method review then identified legacy allocation, registration, prefix inspection and arbitrary request seams; the current handoff classifies and gates every base storage operation. Final runtime review found existing entrypoint child lease calls outside the storage class; DAG wiring must skip or replace them without changing fixed-P2.
